question: A dealer marks an article 60% above the cost price and sells it to a customer allowing two successive discounts of 10% and 20% on the marked price. If he gains Rs. 1,064 in the transaction, the cost price (in Rs.) of the article is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let CP = 100 units ⇒ MP = 160 units (60% above CP).

Successive discounts of 10% and 20% on MP means SP = 160 × 0.90 × 0.80 = 115.2 units.

Profit gained = SP − CP = 115.2 − 100 = 15.2 units.

Since 15.2 units = ₹1064 ⇒ 1 unit = 1064 ÷ 15.2 = 70.

Cost Price = 100 units = 100 × 70 = ₹7000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup % = 60%

Discounts = 10% and 20%

Gain (Profit) = ₹1064

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (1 + Markup% ÷ 100)

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − D₁ ÷ 100) × (1 − D₂ ÷ 100)

Profit = SP − CP
